description: Classify the release impact of one merged pull request.

params.pr: Pull request metadata and actual unified diff: title, description, labels, changed file paths, URL, and diff content (possibly truncated when very large).

impact.instructions: Choose the single highest user-facing release impact of this merged pull request. Analyze the actual code diff first, using the title, description, labels, and changed file paths as supporting context. Cite concrete changed behavior from the diff in your reasoning. Do not infer a feature from implementation-only work. If the diff is truncated, binary-only, empty, or does not provide enough evidence to determine impact, choose review. If the evidence is ambiguous, contradictory, or could plausibly imply a breaking change, choose review.

criteria.major: A change that breaks compatibility for existing users, configuration, data, APIs, or supported workflows. Choose only when a breaking change is explicitly evidenced.
criteria.minor: A new user-facing capability or meaningful additive behavior that remains backward-compatible.
criteria.patch: A user-facing bug fix, reliability improvement, performance improvement, or compatible maintenance change worth shipping.
criteria.none: Documentation-only, tests-only, CI-only, dependency or internal changes with no meaningful user-facing impact.
criteria.review: The available evidence is ambiguous, insufficient, contradictory, or suggests possible compatibility risk that cannot be established confidently.
